product_definition: A.T.O.M is a local-first, open-source workspace for comparing small urban cellular-network configurations on real maps using deterministic RF planning estimates and bounded azimuth search.
primary_label: Deterministic urban RF planning and experimentation workspace.

verdict.label: SCIENTIFIC CLAIM-BOUNDARY DEFECT
verdict.rationale: C — SCIENTIFIC CLAIM-BOUNDARY DEFECT. The primary runtime/README support a coherent, scientifically careful small-plan comparison product, but current unarchived docs/overview.md materially presents vendor antenna validation across terrain/buildings, beamforming work and broad data/performance/scalability claims beyond released evidence. It is not linked from the current docs hub, but is public repository product copy and is not a frozen historical qualification/design report. This cluster of present-tense applicability assertions crosses the locked C rule; it is more than an isolated aspirational roadmap sentence. B describes the core product/workflow condition but is insufficient as the overall claim-alignment verdict. A is contradicted by these claims and other copy drift; D is not supported because the core loop is connected; E is unnecessary because the relevant sources/checks are available. No core RF equation defect or measured accuracy is asserted by this verdict.

terminology: Cell
One selected inventory/planning RF record with its own profile and direction.
Current UI uses Cell; backend tower DTOs and historical reports retain tower. Counting records does not count physical sites.
tower
Legacy/API/data representation of a planning record/location.
API errors still say selected towers; docs sometimes say choose a tower. Avoid translating this into surveyed infrastructure truth.
sector
Directional RF analysis/configuration associated with a Cell.
Single-sector mode and duplicated co-located sectors do not establish a site inventory hierarchy.
site
Candidate planning location or measurement site depending on context.
recommend-sites/Candidate Site docs can sound like greenfield siting; source uses known unselected records. Measurement site IDs have another evidence role.
network
The finite selected group of configured Cells.
Not the whole operator RAN or complete interference environment.
RF profile
Resolved per-Cell radio assumptions with request defaults and explicit overrides.
Distinct from deployment resource Profile A.
propagation / coverage
Modeled received power, usable ray reach, building service or sampled surfaces.
Legacy objective coverage is reach, not continuous geographic coverage. Display labels improve this but API names remain.
interference
Modeled finite-horizon co-channel linear power ledger and quality conversion.
Measure network overlap in tool description should be read as estimate; no measured UE state.
optimization / solution
Feasible azimuth candidate search and one discovered configuration.
Optimal API field and maximum coverage sentence are broader than search/weighted demand semantics.
recommendation
Either optimizer preferred configuration or ranked candidate record.
Both defensible; different task and cap. Needs context, not automatic renaming.
measurement validation
Ordinary CSV residual/global-bias workflow; isolated reference ledger; canonical validation library.
Three distinct evidence paths. UI capability is not proof that the shipped model passed real-campaign validation.
W1
Frozen workload/layout/settings class in historical qualification.
Evidence vocabulary, not model confidence or a universal certification class.
Profile A
2 CPU/4 GiB reference deployment envelope in the locked qualification.
Not RF profile or arbitrary minimum hardware guarantee.
Auto
Resource/admission observation metadata, with estimator admission paused.
Different from Auto-Optimize Sector, which explicitly runs azimuth search.
Project / Scenario / Version / Run
Workspace container / hypothesis / immutable input revision / execution evidence.
Coherent lineage, but unsaved Version and autosaved draft sound contradictory without explanation.

phases.title: Baseline / freeze
phases.finding: Initial shell observation: clean main at e84210dda6fb282474eda4e935f50c598fad7b34, VERSION 0.12.1, empty diff stat. The later freeze-time status includes only the newly created audit directory. Criteria were locked before evaluation; SHA256 4035e4a3ce4cde804a161c7deef9f5061ddaaa29e006b7bad18f4f5934a8cd91. All 3,217 tracked files are hashed, with backend/frontend/science/policy/persistence/OpenAPI/docs/VERSION group identities. No production writes are authorized. Historical shipping-source comparison matches 82/82 source identities; toolchain/dependency/frontend/docs changes do not certify a new resource envelope.

phases.title: Define the product in one sentence
phases.finding: A.T.O.M is a local-first, open-source workspace for comparing small urban cellular-network configurations on real maps using deterministic RF planning estimates and bounded azimuth search. README, docs, app and Product Compass share this thesis. README engine language and acronym density are more technical than necessary; first useful decision is less prominent than features. Git remote identifies Berk-Unsal/atom; no GitHub About description was present in the inspected tracked metadata, and live GitHub metadata was not fetched. An unarchived docs/overview.md contradicts the main thesis by presenting vendor antenna validation across terrain, beamforming experimentation, complete data and universal-region performance. Its Current v1.0 roadmap is also stale. It is not linked from the current landing/search navigation, which reduces exposure but does not make it a protected historical qualification report.

phases.title: Actual users
phases.finding: Primary users are engineers making bounded comparisons and telecom learners/researchers inspecting assumptions; experimenters, systems engineers and contributors are secondary. Evidence supports no operator/enterprise workflow claim. Personas below distinguish supported jobs from reasonable unmet expectations. Overview lists operators/equipment vendors/urban planners more broadly than supported workflows; those personas are aspirational or conditional, not established current customers.

phases.title: Use-case clarity
phases.finding: The defensible job is comparing a small configured urban plan, seeing trade-offs, explaining a recommendation and preserving evidence. Supported uses are classified below. The supplied “what is the use case?” comment is a product-clarity signal only. A broad capabilities catalogue answers what the software contains better than why a newcomer should perform its first comparison.

phases.title: First 30 seconds
phases.finding: Heuristic inspection, not a timed user study: the fresh live app shows Telecom planning, a single Cell,5G / 28 GHz, UMa model, Run needed, a visible Run Sector action, Setup and four stages. A newcomer can identify a map-based RF tool and first compute action; intended decision, source data certainty and accuracy boundary are less visible until disclosures/Data/docs. README identifies engineers/students and estimates; docs hero says inspect/run/model before a user outcome. A simulator/planner/optimizer combination is discoverable but not yet one crisp first-use promise.

phases.title: End-to-end workflow
phases.finding: The primary loop is intentional and connected. Trace below combines current source, regression/browser checks and retained historical real eight-Cell F28 evidence. The present browser workflow suites use mocked APIs; Go tests exercise real engine/controlled geometry; live inspection used the full Ankara backend only for first-screen/navigation observation. This audit did not rerun the costly frozen operational matrix or claim a fresh real-backend eight-Cell browser qualification. Dead ends are local and explicit: no retained Version for Apply, unsupported 140 GHz analyses, independent tool caps, deadlines and export guards.

phases.title: Tool information architecture
phases.finding: Four stages and task-specific progressive disclosures provide real hierarchy; major capabilities are not all permanent peers. Core Lab and deep references can distract when discovered without a planning question, but their optional/isolated scope is valuable and not grounds for deletion. Data carries both source provenance and measurement experiments; Results has several meanings. Preserve current hierarchy and teach the core route before considering new navigation.

phases.title: Terminology
phases.finding: Cell is the selected RF record; tower is a legacy/API/data alias; sector is a directional configuration; site is contextual, not verified infrastructure. These must not be normalized by assumption. Coverage may mean ray reach, building service or sampled surface; optimization changes azimuth, and optimal is bounded. RF profile, Profile A and Auto have distinct meanings. Terminology inventory follows.

phases.title: Scientific claim inventory
phases.finding: The atomic claim matrix below assigns exactly one A–F primary level to each of 56 claim families. The lexical appendix inventories 3,330 matching textual occurrences in 184 files, including generated duplicates and historical reports; validation of input/schema or software is not RF accuracy. Historical qualification/design claims remain attributed to their original scope, never rewritten as present product guarantees. Standards basis is traced to current implementation/citations/fixtures; this is not an independent standards-conformance certification.

phases.title: RF model boundaries
phases.finding: 2.6/28 GHz use the deterministic outdoor UMa path-loss subset with height-aware centerline LOS/NLOS and explicit legacy fallback. Unknown roof evidence is conservative NLOS. Urban NLOS does not get an extra legacy wall penalty.140 GHz is a research attenuation profile with isolated standards references, not canonical radio quality. Building entry is a representative zero-depth facade estimate. Antennas are analytic/single-element references, receiver assumptions scalar/manual or derived. Terrain is optional path-profile evidence and absent from canonical fast RF. Main detailed limits are sound; the landing FSPL/walls summary is stale.

phases.title: Measurement-validation status
phases.finding: The current sanitized real-pilot readiness says real_data_ingested_serving_semantics_blocked: 53,005 raw data rows parsed, zero malformed/dropped samples, 1,858 elapsed-order warnings, 83 registered-flag rows all with NONE connection status, 37 collector serving-change events, and zero canonical observations. Exact pack mapping is absent. B7 bandwidth/resource association, 2.665 versus 2.600 GHz, transmitter/receiver/LOS truth remain separate blockers. No canonical pilot residual artifact or defensible MAE/RMSE resulted. Ordinary CSV diagnostics, isolated research ledger and canonical campaign library are separate capabilities. The later 6A.1.2 reconciliation confirms 37/37 event/candidate transitions, but all 83 registered candidates still conflict with CONNECTION_NONE and 156 PS registration contexts have a valid but contradictory PCI 0. Current readiness remains A_SEMANTICS_UNRESOLVED; event consistency does not authorize promotion.

phases.title: Model accuracy wording
phases.finding: Current main copy explicitly says planning estimate and excludes field/UE/PHY calibration. Accurate/precise language found in current overview material is chiefly a negated limit, future contribution example, coordinate precision or software/data validation. Dangerous exceptions: unconditional validated-sounding bias heading on an ineligible result; maximum-coverage/optimal sector prose; old unscoped parallelization timings. Verified RF follow-up refers to request authorization, not verified physical RF. Do not infer accuracy from standards citations, regression tests, hash equality or operating within resource budgets. The current Project Overview adds a material exception: equipment-vendor antenna validation across terrain/buildings and beamforming prototyping are presented as use cases without a historical/aspirational scope label. Combined with complete-data, sub-100ms and any-region scaling language, this crosses the locked applicability boundary despite modern caveats elsewhere.

phases.title: Eight-Cell claim boundary
phases.finding: Normal network 8 is source/test/API behavior. Operational evidence is the exact frozen paired Ankara 2026.07 W1 layouts,2.6/28 GHz,120 rays / 400 m / 30 dBm / 120°, legacy two-pass, historical Go 1.26.6 Linux/arm64 Profile A 2 CPU/4 GiB. No W2/W3, arbitrary hardware/datasets, stronger models or multi-instance qualification follows. Current README explicitly states limits; no blanket arbitrary-eight certification was found. Current capability reference incorrectly understates the cap as 6.

phases.title: Performance claims / causal attribution
phases.finding: Recorded affected six-Cell 28 GHz request: uncached 94.707–112.731 s; corrected same-container controls 6.720739/6.760776/6.749160 s.434 network proposals preserved;2,604 contribution requests reduced to 180 expensive misses with 2,424 hits. Five distinct profiles/locations among six IDs matter. Scheduling, workers and candidate parallelism were unchanged. The evidence isolates contribution reuse as the correction; no controlled factorial split quantifies caching versus all historical concurrency/other improvements. The supplied Reddit question prompts this check and is not proof.

phases.title: Benchmark communication
phases.finding: Historical deadline report responsibly gives payload, band, rays, radius, toolchain, hardware, quotas, before/after, tiny samples and confounders. It measures admitted requests, not the complete user journey; map refresh, persistence and dataset load have separate cost. Request-local memoization is rebuilt per request, not a persistent cross-request warm cache. Whole-system cold/warm/runtime effects were not controlled enough to promise a universal number. Algorithms 36 s → 250 ms / 4× prose has none of the required context and is unsupported as a released benchmark. Profile A 11.788 s worst request and 1.217 GB kernel peak belong to the separate matrix, not this speedup comparison. Overview adds an unsupported sub-100ms beamforming-adjustment response claim without workload or hardware context. Current UI responsiveness and retained request benchmarks do not establish it.

phases.title: Resource qualification
phases.finding: Profile A is a reference qualification, not a universal minimum system requirement. Frozen W1/paired layouts/settings, single-instance/Linux/arm64 cgroupv2/CGO0, historical Go 1.26.6, fixed concurrency 2/1,60 s deadline and worker 1 / queue 16 define the envelope. Recorded promotion worst request11.788444160 s, minimum headroom 48.211555840 s and process-lifetime kernel peak 1,217,204,224 bytes with no OOM/kill/max events are historical measurements. The current toolchain is 1.26.9; source equality and race tests do not requalify its resource/performance binary.

phases.title: Request-budget UX
phases.finding: 20 ordinary attempts per ClientIP / anchored 60 s plus 8 shared verified eligible follow-up units enables the declared normal map/azimuth journeys without teaching capability accounting to users. Prebooking/fail-closed tests support avoiding budget-exhausted partial eligible fan-out, not guaranteeing all RF work succeeds. API docs should carry counters/headers, architecture docs ownership/verification details, UI the problem and wait/retry action. Current error text distinguishes capacity/budget, but Retry-After is only stored on Error and catches display message. NAT sharing and charged failures can surprise users; no automatic retry or admission redesign is recommended here.

phases.title: Eight-Cell product limit UX
phases.finding: Setup shows selected count, minimum 2 / maximum 8 and refuses a ninth without RF. This feels intentional as a product limit, but the reason is mostly discoverable in README/qualification rather than at the point of selection. The useful explanation is a currently supported small-plan operational scope; users do not need W1/Profile A internals to select Cells. Eight is not a scientific law or guarantee of accuracy.

phases.title: Independent cap coherence
phases.finding: Normal 8, Recommendation existing-input 5, Measurement 1–6 are deliberately independent and remain unchanged. README current scope table is clear. Candidate UI guard/explanation uses 5 and requires a drawn area; app flow further requires at least 2 existing inputs although endpoint supports its own minimum. Measurement UI advertises 5,000 samples but not max 6 and its handler lacks a maximum precheck, so an eight-Cell user encounters a backend rejection. Document this as recoverable workflow debt, not an argument to equalize caps.

phases.title: Results / explainability
phases.finding: Results answers what happened through scores/raw metrics; baseline impact and comparisons show compared with what; thresholds and conditional per-Cell effects show why; non-dominated Solutions support trade-offs. Is it good requires user priorities and policy context:64/100 is neither 64% coverage nor accuracy. Objective meanings and raw denominators are present but not automatically understood. Current empty/infeasible states avoid success claims. Next-inspection guidance exists per tool but is less unified than the evidence itself.

phases.title: Optimization semantics
phases.finding: Default network search is deterministic two-pass coordinate azimuth search on 10° candidates;578 proposals for 8 Cells. Other radio/geometry inputs stay fixed. Priorities weight normalized available utilities, hard constraints gate feasibility; radio quality opt-in starts at 0. Opt-in multistart/archive searches are bounded heuristics. A retained Pareto set is discovered, truncated and not global; local priority reranking is not new RF search. UI/report recommendation wording is substantially honest; single-sector API optimal/max coverage sentence is overbroad and conflates weighted demand with coverage.

phases.title: Uncertainty / provenance
phases.finding: Strong current principle: static source licenses/hashes, observed_tag vs levels-derived vs unknown roof evidence, requested/applied models, applicability/fallback, receiver/quality/building thresholds, Run/Version lineage and report hashes remain explicit. Data calls demand heuristic, not subscriber measurements. Unknown fields remain unsupported/missing rather than promoted. Absolute accuracy uncertainty is not quantified by deterministic repeatability; the real-pilot block is preserved. A report hash proves artifact integrity only.

phases.title: Errors / empty states
phases.finding: Empty states suggest select Cells/run analysis/import samples; unsupported 140 GHz quality is explicit. Stale/historical result badges and unavailable Apply states preserve evidence boundaries. Cap errors and persistence errors are real failures, not success banners. Recovery gaps: Measurement 6 surfaces after submission, generic resource-budget export wording does not teach which artifact to reduce, and retry metadata is not translated into a wait. Browser/Go tests support representative paths; no exhaustive failure-mode or formal accessibility certification was performed.

phases.title: Report / export honesty
phases.finding: HTML and Markdown builders retain selected Cells, request/model/dataset/application metadata, source Runs/Versions, score/baseline/Pareto evidence and limitations. Reports say deterministic planning estimate, not measurement or deployment approval; scalar correction is not full calibration; conditional effects are noncausal. Missing data has explicit unavailable representation. Report maps sample rays for readability with disclosure; full result preservation belongs to bounded project/artifact storage, not the map image. Some exact identity/hash evidence is in retained artifact/source data rather than every printable summary. No claim of complete universal portable evidence is warranted. Portable project files do not include the separate Run History database, generated report files or coverage surfaces; retained Scenario artifacts and embedded Version/Run metadata are narrower than a complete workspace backup. Download reports separately. These documented exclusions should be visible when promising portability.

phases.title: Persistence expectations
phases.finding: Known historical eight-Cell network-result-only round-trip is supported, and current regression suite preserves it.16 MiB file,250k encoded-node,32 MiB/1M decoded-content guards remain. Oversize export throws before download; this audit found no evidence that a rejected export is reported as safely exported. Only recent scenario layers are cached, older inputs remain and require rerun. Draft autosave, immutable Version and downloadable project are different promises. Current README caveat is honest, but discoverability/recovery remain medium debt. The project-format contract explicitly excludes the separate Run History database, generated reports, coverage surfaces and transient view/Undo state. This is documented omission, not silent retention of every important artifact; a saved-local indicator alone does not explain portable backup completeness.

phases.title: README verdict
phases.finding: Good scoped technical introduction and strong scientific caveats; visible scope table, versioned gallery, LFS/Docker/readiness path, settings-first sample, limitations and contribution links. It primarily sells a large capability set after its overview, rather than leading with one concrete comparison problem/outcome. Screenshots demonstrate results/control density more than the complete first planning decision. Source-build/LFS friction is explicit and appropriate; no turnkey operator workflow is implied by the strongest caveats. Its strongest introduction should be retained; inconsistent legacy Overview claims are a separate public-copy defect, not evidence that this README makes those claims.

phases.title: Docs landing verdict
phases.finding: Clear run locally CTA, one planning loop and a prominent confidence boundary lower on the page; search/navigation and light/dark behavior pass current browser checks. Architecture is a peer first destination, so internal system explanation competes with first user outcome. Default propagation sentence is stale, current capability link leads to a 2–6 understatement, and theme previews differ in UI generation. Appearance itself does not invalidate the hierarchy; matched content and a concrete first task matter more than another palette change.

phases.title: Screenshot story
phases.finding: Inspected all four README gallery images and both docs hero assets in place. Network workspace: selection/order, rays and map key. Propagation drawer: configure beam/radius/rays plus explicit Optimize. Optimization results:64.3/100, deltas, raw denominators and discovered trade-offs; no first-selection or full apply/export action. Single-sector: alternative simpler mode and research disclosures. They partially tell configure→analyze→optimize→understand, but start in populated states and omit the initial question/baseline/export decision. Light hero is an older UI capture; dark hero is the current eight-Cell workspace. Captions do not establish measured performance or accuracy.

phases.title: Public positioning
phases.finding: Primary label: deterministic urban RF planning and experimentation workspace. Secondary: cellular-network simulator (planning estimates), bounded azimuth optimization tool, geospatial RF visualization/explanation tool. Research/reference platform describes the optional specialist area. A universal network planner,6G validated simulator or commercial operator-planning replacement is not defensible. The small-scale urban focus is an asset to preserve. Overview currently implies a broader vendor/operator validation tool; treat that mismatch as a claim defect, not a reason to invent enterprise features.

phases.title: Commercial-tool expectation gap
phases.finding: Table distinguishes present, partial, absent and explicitly out-of-scope capabilities. Inventory fields are not an operator integration, configured loading is not capacity, terrain diagnostics are not canonical terrain propagation, CSV ingestion is not field validation, and Core overlays are not mobility/handover prediction. These are expectation boundaries, not an automatic feature wishlist.

phases.title: External feedback synthesis
phases.finding: Only supplied summaries were used. No Reddit thread/author/date or statistically representative audience evidence was provided; none was fetched or invented. Caching question matches repository evidence, use-case question reinforces first-use review, smooth-map praise is preservation input, and small urban scope is source-supported. There are no attributable planner feature requests to justify a new specialist capability.

phases.title: Product debt inventory
phases.finding: Fifteen evidence-backed items below separate claim/documentation drift, workflow discoverability, terms, persistence expectations and integration readiness. None authorizes implementation. Strict OpenAPI integration is blocked; local core planning is not shown to be broken. Field-accuracy and calibration promotion are separately blocked by scientific evidence, not a missing UI feature.

phases.title: Scientific debt inventory
phases.finding: Scientific debt is chiefly unusable measurement evidence and unknown transmitter/resource/receiver truth. Model applicability is explicit; canonical terrain absence and advanced channel/PHY omissions are declared scope limitations, not automatically defects. Do not turn synthetic tests, source identity or operational success into a measured accuracy result.

phases.title: What not to build next
phases.finding: Do not promote 10/12 Cells: no demonstrated user decision blocked by 8, and current independent/persistence limits do not disappear with a cap increase. Do not expand W2/W3 or repeat infrastructure qualification by default: W1 evidence is adequate for the declared use and no broader demand case exists. Do not reopen adaptive admission: invalid estimator validation remains historical evidence and Auto stays observation-only. Do not add arbitrary RF models, universal terrain/clutter physics or an enterprise wishlist without applicability, data and user-task evidence. These are defer decisions, not claims such work can never matter.

phases.title: Ranked next-phase options
phases.finding: Five directions, ranked by evidence and dependency readiness, appear below. Costs/risks are qualitative, not schedule estimates. Current claim reconciliation comes first because the final source pass found material unsupported applicability statements; the first-decision walkthrough follows. Real scientific validation remains high-value but externally blocked. The strict API schema defect is a concrete separate integration task; none authorizes implementation now.

phases.title: Single recommendation
phases.finding: Choose exactly one initiative: reconcile current public claims with the released planning scope. Start with the unarchived Overview vendor/terrain/beamforming/data/performance assertions, then reconcile current algorithm/capability/API/UI wording against the frozen claim matrix. Preserve historical qualification/design reports as evidence. This is a bounded claim-alignment task, not a product redesign, new model, cap expansion or measured-validation claim. A reproducible first-decision example is the next-ranked initiative rather than a substitute for correcting unsupported assertions.

phases.title: Final claim matrix
phases.finding: The matrix is compact by atomic claim family, with source/wording, one category, support judgment, required qualification and recommended wording. Recommended wording is audit output only and has not been applied. Unsupported inferred claims are explicitly marked as absent/inferred rather than falsely attributed to current README.

phases.title: Product workflow scorecard
phases.finding: Ordinal 1–5 scores use the locked anchors. They are auditor judgments from source, tests and bounded visual observation, not measured usability percentages; no arithmetic overall score is manufactured.

phases.title: Audit verdict
phases.finding: C — SCIENTIFIC CLAIM-BOUNDARY DEFECT. The primary runtime/README support a coherent, scientifically careful small-plan comparison product, but current unarchived docs/overview.md materially presents vendor antenna validation across terrain/buildings, beamforming work and broad data/performance/scalability claims beyond released evidence. It is not linked from the current docs hub, but is public repository product copy and is not a frozen historical qualification/design report. This cluster of present-tense applicability assertions crosses the locked C rule; it is more than an isolated aspirational roadmap sentence. B describes the core product/workflow condition but is insufficient as the overall claim-alignment verdict. A is contradicted by these claims and other copy drift; D is not supported because the core loop is connected; E is unnecessary because the relevant sources/checks are available. No core RF equation defect or measured accuracy is asserted by this verdict.

phases.title: No implementation / freeze
phases.finding: End at findings. VERSION stays 0.12.1; all original tracked source, scientific/policy/persistence files, historical evidence and release metadata remain hash-identical. No caps/models/worker/deadline/admission/search/Pareto/Auto changes, README rewrite, changelog edit, tag, release, commit or push. Only the requested Markdown/JSON report and audit support/evidence directory are created. No recommendation is implemented.

methodology.observed_live: Normal Go 1.26.9 backend/full Ankara pack, ignored built frontend, fresh browser origin127.0.0.1:18081. Setup/first-screen/navigation observed with CUA; screenshot inspected. No field measurement or performance benchmark performed.

Draft B verdict was revised to C before completion when the required overview-source pass found material current applicability claims; initial draft report filenames were corrected before delivery. Neither draft was treated as final evidence.

No controlled caching-vs-concurrency factorial study, universal benchmark or full cold/warm decomposition.
No usable canonical field observations, exact transmitter truth or measured residual accuracy.
No raw private campaign copied; sanitized repository readiness summaries audited, not independently re-parsed private bytes.
No live GitHub About description, Reddit thread, author attribution or independent commercial-user demand study.

The historical promotion archive and SHA index are absent at their recorded local paths; committed qualification summaries and current source/regression evidence were checked, but historical raw numeric measurements were not independently reverified. See frozen-evidence-availability.json.

required_final_items.title: Current product one-sentence definition
required_final_items.answer: A.T.O.M is a local-first, open-source workspace for comparing small urban cellular-network configurations on real maps using deterministic RF planning estimates and bounded azimuth search.

required_final_items.title: Primary users
required_final_items.answer: RF/RAN engineers making small-plan comparisons; telecom students/researchers; experimenters, systems engineers and contributors as secondary users.

required_final_items.title: Core use cases
required_final_items.answer: Configure/evaluate small urban plans, inspect propagation/interference, compare azimuth recommendations, explain trade-offs and retain/export evidence.

required_final_items.title: First 30 seconds verdict
required_final_items.answer: RF planning/map tool and Run Sector are visible; first decision, data certainty and accuracy boundary need more guidance.

required_final_items.title: Primary workflow verdict
required_final_items.answer: Coherent main loop; cap/Version/export prerequisites cause recoverable friction. Current mocked browser checks and controlled Go tests supplement retained real F28 evidence.

required_final_items.title: Tool IA verdict
required_final_items.answer: Four stages and progressive disclosure work; optional Core/research breadth needs task context, not deletion.

required_final_items.title: Terminology findings
required_final_items.answer: Cell/tower/site/sector differ by context; coverage is overloaded; RF profile≠Profile A; Auto observer≠Auto-Optimize; optimal is bounded.

required_final_items.title: Scientific claim inventory
required_final_items.answer: 56 atomic claim families, exactly one A–F category each; lexical occurrence appendix and evidence paths retained.

required_final_items.title: 2.6 GHz status
required_final_items.answer: C: documented deterministic UMa planning subset; not field-validated.

required_final_items.title: 28 GHz status
required_final_items.answer: C: documented deterministic UMa planning subset; no calibrated multipath/beamforming claim.

required_final_items.title: 140 GHz status
required_final_items.answer: D: research/reference overlay; ordinary radio quality unsupported.

required_final_items.title: Measurement-validation status
required_final_items.answer: Software tooling exists; real pilot parsed 53,005 rows but yielded 0 canonical observations because serving semantics and truth/resource gates failed.

required_final_items.title: Real-world accuracy status
required_final_items.answer: E: unestablished; no defensible canonical field MAE/RMSE result.

required_final_items.title: Eight-Cell claim boundary
required_final_items.answer: Normal cap 8; only frozen Ankara W1/2.6 & 28 GHz/legacy settings and historical Profile A qualification; no arbitrary networks/W2/W3.

required_final_items.title: Optimization-performance evidence
required_final_items.answer: Affected six-Cell 28 GHz request ≈95–113 s uncached → 6.72–6.76 s corrected in recorded container controls; not a full-workflow guarantee.

required_final_items.title: Caching vs concurrency conclusion
required_final_items.answer: 434 proposals retained; expensive independent Cell computations 2604→180. Reuse is the demonstrated correction; workers/scheduling unchanged; no universal causal percentage split.

required_final_items.title: Benchmark communication findings
required_final_items.answer: Detailed historical audit is scoped; Algorithms 36 s → 250 ms / 4× claims lack workload/hardware/raw evidence and are unsupported.

required_final_items.title: Profile A claim boundary
required_final_items.answer: 2 CPU/4 GiB refers to the frozen historical Go 1.26.6 Linux/arm64 W1 reference, not minimum universal requirements or a new 1.26.9 certificate.

required_final_items.title: Budget-policy UX finding
required_final_items.answer: Normal users need problem/wait/retry guidance, not capability accounting; Retry-After is captured but not presented; NAT shares limits.

required_final_items.title: Eight-Cell UX finding
required_final_items.answer: Count/minimum/maximum/ninth refusal clear; operational reason is mainly in docs.

required_final_items.title: Independent-cap UX finding
required_final_items.answer: README 8/5/6 table clear; Recommendation 5 guard exists; Measurement 6 maximum not disclosed/prechecked before submission.

required_final_items.title: Results/explainability finding
required_final_items.answer: Strong baseline/metrics/conditional effects/trade-offs; /100 is a preference score needing context, not percent accuracy/coverage.

required_final_items.title: Optimization-semantics finding
required_final_items.answer: Azimuth-only bounded search; no global guarantee. Single-sector optimal/max-coverage API sentence overstates semantics.

required_final_items.title: Provenance finding
required_final_items.answer: Strong model/dataset/height/default/fallback/Run lineage; missing truth remains missing. Artifact hashes do not prove physical accuracy.

required_final_items.title: Error/empty-state finding
required_final_items.answer: Most actions and unsupported/stale states are clear; retry wait, oversize recovery and Measurement 6 need improvement.

required_final_items.title: Report/export finding
required_final_items.answer: Retained lineage, selected Cells, model/dataset identity and limits survive; report map ray sampling is disclosed.

required_final_items.title: Persistence expectation finding
required_final_items.answer: Eight result-only round-trip supported within 16 MiB encoded/32 MiB decoded and 1M-node guards. Project exports exclude separate Run History, report files and coverage surfaces; draft/Version/export promises differ.

required_final_items.title: README verdict
required_final_items.answer: Strong scoped technical intro and run path; feature catalogue outweighs one decision/outcome story.

required_final_items.title: Docs landing-page verdict
required_final_items.answer: Useful loop/limits/CTA and working themes; legacy-model summary, stale capability cap and mismatched hero captures need later correction.

required_final_items.title: Screenshot-story verdict
required_final_items.answer: Shows configured maps, controls and optimization impact; lacks a complete first-question/baseline/apply/export narrative; light hero is older.

required_final_items.title: Recommended primary product label
required_final_items.answer: Deterministic urban RF planning and experimentation workspace.

required_final_items.title: Commercial-tool expectation gap
required_final_items.answer: Inventory, drive-test, terrain/clutter, antenna and calibration are partial; PCI/neighbor planning absent; mobility/capacity/live control outside scope.

required_final_items.title: External-feedback synthesis
required_final_items.answer: Use-case question=messaging signal; caching=technical question supported by source; smooth UI=praise, not a frame-rate study; small urban focus=source-supported strength.

required_final_items.title: Product-debt inventory
required_final_items.answer: 15 items with evidence, impact, severity, blockers and fix-soon fields in the report/JSON.

required_final_items.title: Scientific-debt inventory
required_final_items.answer: Measured validation, transmitter truth, receiver/resource/frequency/LOSmetadata and calibration evidence are missing/blocked; canonical terrain is a declared limitation.

required_final_items.title: What NOT to build next
required_final_items.answer: No 10/12 Cell promotion, W2/W3 expansion, more qualification by default, adaptive admission reopening or arbitrary new RF models.

required_final_items.title: Ranked next-phase options
required_final_items.answer: 1 claim-boundary reconciliation; 2 first planning decision; 3 canonical validation prerequisites; 4 strict API contract integrity; 5 portable evidence/report clarity.

required_final_items.answer: Reconcile current public claims with released planning scope
